articleTitle: GA-based parameterization and feature selection for automatic music genre recognition
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Automatic music genre recognition can be done by collaborative filtering or by content-based filtering. In collaborative filtering the music is classified on the basis of the similarity to pieces already classified by users - it is implicitly assumed that the users have proper knowledge to recognize music genres. The second approach - the content-based filtering - is based on extracting sound features directly from music and using them for classification. This study presents a content-based classification system designed to assign music tracks to genres. The classification process is done by 2 classifiers: a feed-forward neural network and k-nearest neighbors algorithm. The structure of the neural network, the number of the nearest neighbors and the actual sound features are selected by a genetic algorithm (GA). The presented approach is tested on a database comprising 10 main genres and 33 subgenres.

articleTitle: Diagnostic signs of induction motor broken rotor bars in electromotive force signal
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A diagnostic coefficient, being the function of the average value of wavelet-decomposition coefficients sum for medium-frequency domain is proposed. A method for its decomposition with the use of the theory of reverse z-transform is worked out. The proposed method made it possible to specify diagnostic signs of IM broken rotor bars in the motor self-running-out mode and determine the degree of the rotor breakage.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic heating in magnetic fluid deep hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the numerical modeling of magnetically induced heating of tissues in magnetic fluid deep hyperthermia. When placed in sinusoidal varying electromagnetic field, the Brownian particle rotation and Néel relaxation mechanisms induce in ferrofluid heat generation. In order to destroy tumors cells while preventing healthy tissues, such parameters as susceptibility of nanoparticles, exciting current parameters and intensity of magnetic fields should be calculated precisely. In this publication, coupled field problem resulting from Maxwell's equation and Penne's bioheat equation is discussed. Both sets of equations are solved using the finite element analysis method. We use a simplified model of human thorax with blood perfusion mechanism and tumor placed in it. Heat generation source in tumor is obtained by ferromagnetic nanoparticles. Magnetic and temperature field distribution is discussed in context of optimal tumor treatment.

articleTitle: Adaptation of discrete macromodels for calculations in MATLAB/Simulink environment
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper discusses the approach how to ensure the stability of procedure for the calculations of electric circuits containing elements described by discrete macromodels.

articleTitle: SAR calculations for titanium bar-implant subjected to microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper describes the assessment of exposure of a six-year-old male patient with a titanium bar implanted after Nuss procedure to microwave radiation with frequency of 2.45 GHz. The local SAR concentrations inside the boy's trunk for two variants of plane wave polarizations with regard to the titanium implant have been considered. It was demonstrated that an analyzed concave bar-implant poses no danger during occupational and environmental exposures according to current safety standards.

articleTitle: Identification of nonlinearities of induction motor equivalent circuits with the use of the instantaneous power method
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A method for identification of induction motor parameters with the use of instantaneous power components balance equations is proposed in the paper. A dependence for nonlinear resistance in the rotor current function is obtained.

articleTitle: Calculation of capacitors for starting up a three-phase asynchronous motor fed by single-phase power supply
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In the article a method for the determination of the capacitance necessary for starting up a three-phase asynchronous motor fed by a single-phase power supply is presented. The method and a calculation algorithm are based on a highly adequate mathematical model of the asynchronous motor which takes into account the magnetic core saturation and current displacement in the rotor bars. The task is solved as the boundary problem for the system of differential equations describing the processes in the engine in phase coordinate axes.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis between the 2D and 3D models of interstitial microwave hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The aim of this study is the comparison of the 2D and 3D finite element time-dependent analysis for interstitial microwave hyperthermia treatment. The described method is based on microwave heating of pathologic human tissue using a thin coaxial-slot antenna placed invasively in the diseased tissue. The shown problem relies on the solving of coupled electromagnetic and thermal fields under the assumption of an axial symmetrical model. The wave equation in a sinusoidal steady state and the bioheat equation under a transient state condition are considered. The numerical calculations for the 2D and 3D models give consistent results with an acceptable level of relative error. Increasing the finite element mesh density for the refined 2D* model leads to a more accurate evaluation of the tissue temperature while reducing computation time.

articleTitle: Automatic recognition of drill condition on the basis of images of drilled holes
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic algorithm to recognize the condition of drills on the basis of analysis of the drilling hole images. The algorithm includes the image preprocessing leading to extraction of the diagnostic features, which are used as the input attributes for the classification system. The condition of drill is classified into two groups: the useful one (the sharp enough state) and worn out (useless in production).

articleTitle: Cell segmentation in desmoglein-3 stained specimen microscopic images using GVF and watershed algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents modification of conventional watershed algorithm for cell segmentation in microscopic images of desmoglein-3 stained specimen. Presented method combines color deconvolution for ihc marker separation and GVF for watershed segmentation. Conventional watershed is highly noise sensitive, which often occurs in microscopy images. Suggested solution considerably reduces over segmentation problem (80-90% cells segmented correctly) and enables further image analysis.

articleTitle: Control model of energy flow in agricultural biogas plant using SCADA software
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents a model of controlling the flow of energy in agricultural biogas plant. Control model was made on the basis of a shared project biogas power plant. Biogas plant control algorithm modeled using SCADA software and an analysis of cost performance and life of the investment have been presented.

articleTitle: Efficiency of wireless power supply in various configurations of coils
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In the article two wireless electrical equipment power supply systems were discussed. The systems containing two and three air-core coils placed in various distances from one another were presented. Tests were conducted with the objective to identify the highest efficiency of the system with the transmission of 5 W to the distance of 50 mm. In the article operation of the systems was examined in the application for transmission to further distances.

articleTitle: Module structure of UAV-based computerized systems for remote environment monitoring of energy facilities
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Article considers modular construction principle of computerized information-measurement systems (CIMS) based on unmanned aerial complexes (UAC) for remote control of energy objects environment. Application examples of different types of variable sensors for environment characteristics remote control are presented. Experimental researches of simultaneous use of different sensor types in CIMS based on UAC with simultaneous data transmission in real time and recording by onboard CIMS subsystem module were conducted.

articleTitle: A comparison of ICNIRP and IEEE guidelines to evaluate low frequency magnetic field localised exposure
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Numerical calculations of exposure to magnetic field of operators of suspended hand-operated resistance welding guns were performed using the own homogeneous, flexible human body models CIOP-MAN of the 95th and 5th percentile of adult men dimensions (185 and 164 cm in height), in 16 exposure situations with various postures of operator - typical for automotive factory. An assessment concerned calculated values of an induced electric field (E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub>) in the brain and the heart - according to the ICNIRP (International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection, 2010) and the IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, 2002). The results show applicability of flexible human body models in exposure evaluation based on E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> values, even homogeneous. The values of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">in</sub> in the brain and the heart are up to 34% higher when calculated following ICNIRP requirements than the values calculated following the IEEE method. The values of a welding current producing a B-field in the heart area of 100 μT/50Hz (i.e. the exposure limit for cardiac pacemakers users provided by ACGIH (American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists, 2016) and CENELEC standard (European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization)) are in the range of 0.43-1.6 kA, which is significantly lower than the typical current used in the industry (5-15 kA). Cardiac pacemaker users should not operate welding guns, as a result of the individual risk assessment required by the European directive on workers' protection (Directive 2013/35/EU).

articleTitle: Use of personal computers with multi-core processors for optimisation using the genetic algorithm method
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In the study the possibilities of using personal computers equipped with multi-core processors for optimisation calculations of complex technical objects were analysed. Desktops and portable computers, such as laptops, were compared. The exemplary object which was subject to the optimisation process was a three-phase, unshielded busduct in constant insulation. A genetic algorithm method was used for the purposes of optimisation. Times and accelerations of calculations obtained thanks to the use of multi-processor technology were compared in the study.

articleTitle: Automatic quantification of vessels in hemorrhoids whole slide images
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the automatic method to examine the histological Whole Slide Images of hemorrhoids. The specimen were stained by Hematoxiline and Eosine, and evaluated by number of vessels, occurrence blood clots and hemorrhage. The proposed method is based on colour deconvolution, mathematical morphology, decision tree classification, region growing operation and region reconstruction. The results of algorithm were compared with medical expert results, what confirmed efficiency of presented algorithm. In 80% of cases, vessels were correctly detected. In 85% cases correctly evaluated occurrence of blood clots and hemorrhages were correctly evaluated in 75% of cases.

articleTitle: Simulation of electric field on the surface of a long flashover arrester
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The aim of the paper is to use computer simulation to analyze the electric field distribution on the surface of loop-shaped long-flashover arrester. The 3D model of the arrester was built in a computer program Comsol. On the basis of the simulation results the device was modified to obtain a better distribution of the electric field. This modification was aimed at cost minimization assuring the high quality of the device.

articleTitle: Identification of diffusion coefficients in heat equation on the base of non-adiabatic measurements of ferrofluids
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article concerns the heat flow problem during magnetic field excitation of superparamagnetic fluid. Precise determination of the energy converted into the heat is important issue defining applicability of the phenomena in the Magnetic Fluid Hyperthermia therapy. However it can be done only when all other heat transfer parameters are known, which often not true. Authors presented method of identification of those parameters by the use of numerical model based on the finite element method. Nearly perfect match with real measurements has been reached with three parameters optimization. Results helped to identify heat leakage which could lead into over 50% underestimation of the thermal energy provided into the ferrofluid.

articleTitle: Wave parameters of symmetrical two-port networks containing elements of fractional order
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss wave parameters, i.e. wave impedance as well as damping and phase transfer coefficient for symmetrical two-port networks containing elements of fractional order with sinusoidal forcing in a steady state. We present the appropriate formulae for two different elements of fractional order in T-type and Π-type two-port network. We conducted numerical experiments on the basis of which the plots of the aforementioned parameters were made as functions of the frequency for the chosen fractional orders. On the basis of these sequences, we formulated the conclusion.

articleTitle: Improvement of segmentation quality of multispectral images by increasing resolution
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper considers increasing of the multispectral images resolution using arithmetic combinations based on the Brovey transform method to improve segmentation of multispectral images by k-means clustering algorithm.

articleTitle: Problems of adequate modelling of radio electronic device parameter distributions
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Increasing the quality requirements for modern radio electronic apparatus for different purposes has emphasized the problem of accuracy assurance by complex optimization of the manufacturing processes. This requires the programmes and models used to be of high flexibility and adequacy. Conventional application of the classical laws of random variable distributions, in most cases, does not satisfy these requirements. The research performed has revealed the possibility of enhancing adequacy of the models of real apparatus parameter distributions in the way of using the multiparametric functions with independent parameters.

articleTitle: Implementation of some iterative matrix solvers in simulation of the wave propagation problem using the time-harmonic finite difference algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this paper, the formulation of two-dimensional finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) for heterogeneous and lossy materials is presented. But the main attention is focus on the efficient formulation of the matrix solver. Contemporary, the numerical models are consisted of a large-scale sparse complex matrix, therefore the specific formulation of the solver enable to improve the properties of the proposed algorithm. Two iterative subroutines for the complex equation are presented and validated, i.e. the BiConjugate Gradient Stabilized method (BiCGStab) and the Generalized Minimum Residual method with restarts (GMRES(m)). The stability and performance of these algorithms are tested using model based on typical building construction including concrete column.

articleTitle: Solving nonograms using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the possibilities of using classical genetic algorithm as a tool for solving logical images. Results are presented for simple objective function taking into account the quantity of 0's and 1's and the modified objective function basing on the differences in length of each filled block. Brute-force algorithm was used to illustrate the complexity of NP-complete problem.

articleTitle: Preliminary study of random variable algebra for biological tissue description
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Parameters of human tissues are subject of a wide variability, where different sources of the uncertainty should be considered. The complexity is far beyond measurements errors, which are typical for technical applications. The paper discusses applicability of the random variable algebra in the numerical modeling of such strongly uncertain objects. Basic operations (sum, product and ratio) on random variables described by probability density function (PDF) are presented. To understand results of 2D finite element model, they have been compared with simple 1D resistors line for which analytical solution could be found. Statistical experiments were conducted using classical Monte Carlo method. In the conclusions authors explain different behavior of the local (maximal values) and the global (total resistance) results for different shapes of conductivity variability.

articleTitle: Accuracy of numerical model of coaxial impulse voltage divider validated with measurements
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents a numerical model and measurements of the high voltage impulse voltage coaxial divider. The numerical simulation are obtained both for two and three dimensional models in COMSOL Multiphysics. The paper discusses the accuracy of an electrostatic numerical model and compares the results with measurements. Numerical experiments are calculated to analyse the precision of assembly of an in-house manufactured voltage divider. Both uncertainty of the simulations due to electric permittivity and precision of the mechanical realisation of the divider are analysed.

articleTitle: Measurement of complex signals by quadrature sampling with filtering
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The study deals with a hardware and software implementation of a system for measurement of complex electric signals by quadrature sampling method with filtering using Altera cyclone III FPGA. Ther FIR filters are computed by weighting method with window functions.

Author Keywords: amplitude and phase of a complex signal

articleTitle: Optimization of process of induction clamping
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Optimization of the process of induction clamping is presented, consisting in finding the optimum shape of the field coil. The objective function takes into account the required expansion of the bore of the clamping head. While the forward problem is, as a coupled task with nonlinear and nonstationary interaction of three physical fields (magnetic field, temperature field and field of thermoelastic displacements), solved by Finite Element Method, the backward problem is solved using several heuristic and deterministic algorithms. The methodology is illustrated with a typical example.

articleTitle: Multiobjective optimization approach to the active power filter control
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The optimisation approach to voltage harmonic elimination and voltage symmetry improving is presented. The parallel filter used for the voltage shape improving in three-phase four wire systems is considered. The nonlinear inductor is applied as a source of current and voltage harmonics. Two cases are considered: harmonic reduction and unbalanced load correction. The multiobjective optimization functions are applied to acquire the reference signal for active power filter control.

Author Keywords: detection of voltage harmonics and coefficient of unbalance

articleTitle: Implementation of the variable density mesh within the finite difference frequency domain algorithm to analysis of electromagnetic field in building constructions
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents the developed algorithm of the finite difference frequency domain method (FDFD). The proposed formulation allows analyzing some large-scale models using a local refinement of the differential mesh based on the h-adaptation of the rectangular elements. The final form of the algorithm is implemented to estimate field phenomena connected with the propagation of high frequency electromagnetic waves in building constructions. The electrical losses in materials caused by conducting and displacement currents are taken into account. The presented algorithm is applied to analyze electromagnetic field around a pillar of a building, in the band of some local wireless communication systems. The results obtained from the proposed FDFD scheme are confronted with the field distribution computed using FDTD and FEM methods.

articleTitle: Composite panels as electromagnetic field shields
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper describes fabrication of laminated panels which were analyzed as protection screen from high frequency electromagnetic field. Three test panels with different structure were designed and investigated on the effectiveness of electromagnetic screening. Investigations were conducted in electromagnetic compatibility laboratory as also verified in numerical way. Obtained results were summarized and conclusions were drawn.

articleTitle: Computer simulation as a way of usable volume estimation in TEM waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Striplines are common waveguides used for susceptibility tests. Standards as 61000-4-20 describe procedures for finding volumes with a uniform, strong electric field, but only for frequencies below the first cut-off frequency of the stripline. For higher frequencies modes other than TEM start to propagate and an analytical determination of the field between a stripline's plates is hard or even impossible (i.e. for non-homogenous interior of the stripline). The solution of electric field in a stripline could be found by means of a numerical approximation (e. g. using Finite Element Method) of Helmholtz equation. In this paper such a numerical simulation is presented. The numerical model is verified against the measurements in the frequency range above the first cut-off frequency of a stripline. On the basis of numerical simulation an electric field is determined in the stripline and a usable volume for an extended frequency range is estimated. Such a numerical simulation can be used to take into account also large metallic objects in the vicinity of the stripline.

articleTitle: Heat flow in installations with photovoltaic tiles
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents methods for determining similarity numbers do define the density of heat flux in a system. An installation was analysed with photovoltaic tiles located on the roof of a building. The values of similarity numbers and heat flux were determined, and the type of the system was defined for the case analysed.

articleTitle: Two-step power supply application to reduce THDi ratio in LED light sources with integrated driver
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents the concept of using a two-stage power supply unit to reduce the harmonic frequencies of electric current generated by light-emitting diodes fitted with an integrated power supply and driver. In the work, there are references to the most important Standards pertaining to generation higher harmonics of current. It also provides information on the experimental setup and the measurement methodology. Subsequently, the paper discusses and analyses the research results. Finally, there are conclusions and observations on the conducted study.

articleTitle: Modeling the processes of dynamics at biogas plants on the acetogenesis stage
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The task of modeling the processes of anaerobic microbiological fermentation with keeping the balance at the acetogenesis stage was considered in this work. It was proposed and justified to build models at these stages in the form of interval discrete dynamic model. The structure identification method of IDDM on the principles of honey bee colony functioning in the food search process, which provides the possibility of obtaining simple IDDDM structures with specified prognostic properties relative to existing methods, was substantiated.

articleTitle: A system of wireless transmission of electric energy with the selection of resonant capacitances
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper discusses the method of selecting compensation capacitances to obtain a high-efficient system of wireless transmission of electric energy. The system with a serial-in-serial-out resonant circuit, an air-core transformer was tested. An attempt was made to select such values of capacitance that the system could operate within a large distance between the windings of the air-core transformer.

articleTitle: Impact of the selected FCG design parameters on the current gain
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents numerical, circuital model of the magnetic flux compression generator. The model was used to study the influence of the selected generator parameters on the current gain ratio. The authors discussed the most important characteristics of the model used as the primary stage of the FCG design. The simulations were carried out using a specially designed model developed in Matlab Simulink.

articleTitle: HER2/CEN17 biomarkers detection in CISH images
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents an algorithm of HER2/CEN17 genes biomarkers detection in CISH images (Chromogenic in situ hybridization) which supports the diagnosis of the breast cancer. The algorithm is based on morphological transformations, the usage of structural elements (strel objects) and application of distance function. The developed transformation increases the contrast between biomarkers and background which makes possible the use of simple threshold methods for final detection of biomarkers.

articleTitle: Combination of induction and laser cladding and its 3D computer model
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: A 3D model of combined induction and laser cladding is presented. This electroheat process is characterized by time-varying geometry because of material added in the form of metal powder in order to form the clad. The paper brings a novel approach to its modeling which required expensive remeshing of the whole investigated domain in every time step. The offered technique is based on local adaptive refinement of the existing mesh that allows detailed mapping of distribution of temperature in the thermally exposed domain and assigning the correct parameters of the present material. In this way it is possible to distinguish both solid and liquid phases and also (after cooling and solidification) the final shape of the clad that is not known in advance. The methodology is illustrated with a typical example whose results are discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of skeletal structures for the pelvis area with the use of 3-dimensional binary thinning algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The article presents the use of 3-dimensional thinning algorithm in creation of skeletal structures describing the area of pelvis and its surrounding. The skeletal descriptors are created for the models of pelvis and femurs and further transformed from its voxel representation into the graph. The result of the skeletonization is compared with the Reeb graphs created for the same bone models. The usefulness of the skeletons for the morphing algorithm is discussed.

articleTitle: The defining of influence on the pollution of the electrodes impact of the conductive controvert cross-sectional fluid flow on its outbound current
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper contains the results of theoretical research compensation of influence on the pollution of the electrodes of conductive transformer of cross-sectional milk flow into milk line. By means of determination the thickness of layer pollution and consideration of its impact on the size of the output cross-sectional area flow.

articleTitle: The current density distribution in the three-phase bus-bars system
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical computation method for determining the current distributions in high-current unshielded three-phase busducts of rectangular busbar. This method consists of using an exact formula of self and mutual inductance.

articleTitle: External optimization of SQL-query under conditions of databases structural uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper deals with factors that influence the speed of data receiving in information systems. The method of automatic external SQL-query optimization is described. The method is based on the principle of building a local model of controlled process. It allows one to optimize the SQL-queries regardless of applied database management system and its settings. The structural and functional diagram of adaptive system of an external SQL-query optimization is presented. Possibility of using the proposed method under the conditions of databases structural uncertainty was tested.

articleTitle: Particle swarm optimization in synthesis of electric circuits
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents application of particle swarm optimization in designing electrical circuits on the basis of frequency characteristics. Particle swarm is a population-based global optimization algorithm, inspired by the behavior of flocks of birds or insect swarming. This algorithm is applied in optimization approach to the synthesis of the electric circuits on the basis of the required frequency characteristics. The usefulness of the algorithm was shown on the example of designing the electrical filter and humidity sensor model. The results prove the practical suitability of PSO to the optimization problems of many minima.

articleTitle: The investigation of the energy characteristics of linear periodically-time-variable circuits by the frequency symbolic method
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The paper presents two new software functions of the system of software functions MAOPCs. The first software function is designed to determine the instantaneous power in the branch of linear periodically-time-variable circuit and the second software function is designed to determine the transfer coefficient of average power from input range to the output. The paper also presents computer experiments of the usage of these functions.

Author Keywords: the system of software functions MAOPC

articleTitle: The system of remote Education Resource Center elements development
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The architecture of remote Education Resource Center for the students of engineering on the basis of data space is developed. The consolidated data catalog and the query processing schemes in data space are proposed.

articleTitle: Simulation studies of electric field distribution in the evaluation of the influence of neighboring conductive infrastructure on field conditions over air terminals
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The influence of the infrastructure around the protected objects on field conditions over air terminals and the localization of strike points are analyzed in the paper. For this aim the theoretical study and simulations of electric field distribution around the surface of conductive structures have been performed.

articleTitle: Sequential pattern recognition for medical records analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: Automatic recognition of patterns is an important problem in a variety of engineering and scientific disciplines. The most common application in medicine relates to medical imaging for diagnostics' purpose. This paper presents another field of pattern recognition application - mining medical records. Analysis of treatment pathways (in which diagnostic and therapeutic procedures are sequenced on a timeline) as a mean of providing and standardized patient care of high quality, is one of the issues gaining in importance in the last decade in the field of medical informatics. As there is a need for scalable computational tools for pattern exploration, we propose a conceptual framework, adapted to Poland's context, for expressing data mining tasks to discover knowledge about patients and providers similarities involving multiple time and procedure granularities.

articleTitle: Examination of the flat contact
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: The object of this work was to study the flat contact heating caused by the continuous current. The current heating study was to determine the constant temperature increments of individual elements of the test high current electric contact. At the same time, in the case of the test electric contact, also in determining whether the measured temperature increments during the flow of rated current do not exceed the limit values laid down by the relevant standards. The research started with a field analysis. The tests were carried out using the ANSYS environment. It is a tool developed for over 40 years that enables modelling and analysing objects using the finite element method. It consists of many software solutions tailored to the needs of the selected simulation. The ANSYS Mechanical Simulation Software was applied to carry out the thermal-electrical analysis. It has all the necessary features to represent the actual physical values in the research. The aim of this study was to raise the problem of the optimal parameter selection of the high current flat formation at which the energy transfer would take place with the greatest efficiency. The physical quantity that has been taken into special consideration in the analysis of different shapes was the temperature - and the distribution of its value in the area of the contact system. The research included in this study may contribute to a better understanding of the phenomena of electricity in conductors, for transmitting high power. An integral part of the flow of electric current is generation of heat. The paper therefore focused in particular on the temperature distribution and the knowledge of the phenomena on which it depends.

articleTitle: Method of reduction for interval system of linear algebraic equations and its application to modeling a small hydroelectric power station
publicationTitle: 2016 17th International Conference Computational Problems of Electrical Engineering (CPEE)
abstract: In this paper we propose a new method for finding approximate solutions of ISLAE, by bringing it to “saturated block” using a procedure of reduction. The method is based on the analysis of the properties of solutions ISLAE and on the analysis of the properties of interval models constructed on the basis of these solutions.

Author Keywords: Interval System of Linear Algebraic Equations (ISLAE)
